Treat classification labels as exact ledger entries, not as suggestions or prose. Keep unrelated operational threads separate from the focal decision. The standing correspondence word is Morrow; this direct fact is unrelated to the earlier classification record.

We are reconciling the lockside worksheet at the east lock. The focal entry concerns one incoming parcel, and the rotation steward has asked us to apply a deterministic rule. Apply priorities in order. The priority notice action comes first and maps to Garnet; the standard notice action comes next and maps to Mallow. The named Orchard Quiet exception suppresses only the first action, after which evaluation continues to the second. Read the mapping literally and retain the exact capitalization of the two possible ledger words. The first unrelated thread concerns canvas-cover inventory: its count was copied from yesterday and will be checked separately. That inventory neither changes a predicate nor selects a classification label.

I have separated the classification rule from the canvas-cover inventory thread. The latter still needs a physical recount before anyone closes its worksheet, but it supplies no input to the focal rule. A second unrelated thread concerns volunteer radio roster. Its appointment was moved to the following week, and the move affects staff availability only. I will preserve both threads as context without using either one as evidence for the focal answer. The operations margin also records who will perform each follow-up and which worksheet will receive the confirmation. Those notes make the conversation realistically interleaved, yet they do not add a criterion, change a comparison, or create an exception.

The audit trail distinguishes the submitted evidence from the calculation that follows, so a reviewer can reconstruct the result without relying on tone or order. This separation prevents an incidental scheduling remark from masquerading as focal data.
